_source: Bridge 2 Fun Training.pdf pp.18-24 — 'Review of Staycation Dec 2025'
_note: Hands transcribed from four-hand diagrams. Suit order S,H,D,C. The 'hcp' field is the number PRINTED on the page next to each seat — an independent checksum the validator compares against the transcribed cards.

deals.lesson: E opens 1C. W should ignore diamonds and bid 1H even with six diamonds and four hearts, with a non-game-forcing hand — bring a major in as soon as possible (bypass diamonds). With a game-forcing hand, bid naturally: longer/higher suit first.
deals.also: After (1c)-(1d), N should double to show a strong hand and plan to bid spades later. E should pass, not bid 1NT to show a weak hand. Play problem: dummy had DJ73 remaining when E played D8 — W should play the 9 if S plays low.

deals.lesson: After (P)-P-(2h)-2s, W should bid 3H — a cuebid showing 10+ points and spade support.
deals.also: 4S makes because the DK is with N. Declarer should take the DA and lead towards the DQ after removing all trumps; you do not need trumps for any ruffs.

deals.lesson: After N opens 1H, S should bid 3H, 4C (splinter) or 2NT (Jacoby 2NT, aggressive). At the table S bid 1NT incorrectly.
deals.also: 6H is hard to reach and too aggressive. Twelve tricks are available by discarding a diamond on the fourth spade; 6H makes only because spades are 3-3.

deals.makeable: NS 6H; S 4S; S 5C; N 3S; N 4C; EW 2D
deals.lesson: After N opens 3H, S should immediately think about slam — two-card heart support is good enough. At the table S bid 3NT incorrectly. Any bid by S is forcing except 3NT and shows heart support. S should just bid 4NT (RKC 1430) and then 6H.
deals.also: Because of the bad heart break you must finesse the SJ to make 6H. Against 3NT, W incorrectly led D8 when a lead from a sequence was available — the correct lead is DK. S should hold up twice.

deals.lesson: South opened 1C. W has a perfect takeout double. At the table S bid 3NT incorrectly.
deals.also: During the play, draw trumps and establish spades; discard two hearts on the spades. At the table W discarded a club incorrectly — the club can be ruffed on the other side and the HQ was a loser.

deals.lesson: After (1s)-2h, W should bid 2NT showing 8-10 points and spade control. With little extra, W should bid 3NT. At the table W passed incorrectly — you can miss an easy game if E has a little extra.
deals.also: Against 2H, S led S7 and W played low. S7 could be a doubleton and it is correct for N not to take the ace right away; N should play the S8. At the table N played the SJ incorrectly, giving a free finesse of the ST.

deals.lesson: It is hard to reach 4H unless both players are aggressive, but you should make ten tricks.
deals.also: E has two spade losers, one of which can be ruffed in the dummy. At the table E drew trumps incorrectly before planning to ruff the spade. Play a low spade from both hands first, then take the SA followed by a spade ruff before drawing trumps. Another source of tricks is clubs: the CK will lose to the ace, but a ruffing finesse of the CQ establishes two club tricks in the dummy.

deals.lesson: After S bids 1D there is no good bid for W — the correct bid is pass. At the table W bid 1NT incorrectly. 1NT shows 15-18 points; 1NT doubled can go down four for -800.
deals.also: After W bid 1NT, N bid 3H (out of syllabus) and S correctly bid 4H.

deals.lesson: The bidding at the table was perfect: 1N-2N; 3N. Unfortunately it goes one down.
deals.also: At the table it went two down because the SK and HA were played before unlocking the clubs. There are only eight top tricks assuming four club tricks are taken properly. The only chance of an extra trick is in spades: play low spades from both hands, since you will lose at least one spade anyway. The issue is this line of play was not attempted — taking the top tricks just concedes defeat without trying.

deals.lesson: After three passes E opened 1D. At the table W incorrectly bid 2NT (correct on points but denies a major suit) instead of 1S. E incorrectly bid 3H — that is a reverse bid. With 14 points E could accept the invite and bid 3NT. The correct contract is 4S.
deals.also: At the table the contract was 4D and S led the DJ incorrectly — S should just wait for their diamond tricks rather than give a free finesse. Try a safer lead, e.g. clubs, which no one had bid.

deals.lesson: The correct contract of 2S was reached after 1N-2h; 2s. On the opening lead of a low diamond, N incorrectly played the DK instead of the DQ. When leading you lead the top of the sequence, but when following you play the lowest of the sequence.
deals.also: E correctly entered the dummy to finesse the SK, but played a low spade towards the SJ. That won, but E could not repeat the finesse. Start the finesse by playing a high card so that you can repeat it if it succeeds.

deals.lesson: Most Norths would open 3C. After two passes W should double for takeout. E could pass this double since NS are vulnerable, bid 3NT (they have a control in clubs and no major), or bid 3D/4D. Passing the double — converting the takeout double into a penalty double — would work best here.
deals.also: A proper defence should limit NS to seven tricks. If N plays a low club, E should play the J to ensure one club trick; at the table E played low incorrectly.

deals.lesson: At the table N incorrectly opened the bidding with 1NT. 1NT should be 15-17. If partner has 6-7 points you may miss a game by bidding 1NT with 19 points.
deals.also: The correct lead is HJ. E can get three heart tricks but forgot that the hearts were good at the end, and misdefended.

deals.lesson: E opened 2D. W correctly bid 2S, which is forcing. E incorrectly passed the forcing 2S bid. E could have three-card spade support and 4S would be a better game contract. E should rebid 3D or raise to 4D/5D.
deals.also: 3NT could make if diamonds are divided 3-2 with at least one honour with N.

deals.lesson: 3NT was reached correctly with 1N-3N. N led H4 (fourth best). W should apply the Rule of 11 and determine that S has only one card higher than the H4. At the table the HQ was played, which would have been incorrect if S held the HK.
deals.also: W should play a low heart from the dummy to see which card S plays; win the HT, then plan to play a low heart towards the HQ to establish it. At the table W simply cashed the top tricks and conceded the rest — W could have made 5NT but made only 3N.
